en.html:
Hikaru's body had been revived.
Yesterday, in that one moment—in a single instant.

The hair that had fallen out. The teeth.
The flesh that had been only skin.
The skeleton like a dry branch.

All of it had grown back, fresh and full of life.

...Naturally, such a thing cannot happen within ordinary reason.

What did it was a power beyond ordinary reason. The power of sword-armor, surely.

A true-forged sword-armor raises the physical ability of its shite by leaps and bounds. Recovery power is included in that.

If a warrior's arm is cut off, it will come back in time, provided it is kept joined. There is even talk that it can grow anew.

So Hikaru's abnormal recovery, seen as the work of a sword-armor, is understandable.

But it was not possible.

Even when it is not worn, even when the two are kept far apart, a true-forged sword-armor does enough to speed up healing of wounds. That much, yes. But that happens only because wielder and sword-armor are tied by a strange bond.

There is an old rite of the warrior houses, called the Tatewaki.
Warrior and sword-armor face each other and question each other's nature, and each accepts the other: one as wielder, one as weapon.

ja.html:
光の肉体は蘇生を遂げていた。
　昨日の、あの刹那――――<ruby>一瞬にして<rt>・・・・・</rt></ruby>。

　抜け落ちていた髪も、歯も、
　皮ばかりであった肉も、
　枯れ枝さながらの骨格も。

　全てが瑞々しく再生していた。

　……無論。
　そのような事が、常理の範疇で起こるわけがない。

　あれを成したのは、常理を超えるちから――
　劒冑の力であろう。

　真打の劒冑は<ruby>仕手<rt>シテ</rt></ruby>……使い手の身体能力を飛躍的に
向上させる。
　その中には回復力も含まれる。

　武者は腕を切り落とされても、<ruby>繋いでおけば<rt>・・・・・・</rt></ruby>やがて
元に戻る。
　<ruby>生え変わる<rt>・・・・・</rt></ruby>ことさえあるという。

　光の見せた異常回復も、劒冑の作用とみれば納得が
いく。
　
　だが有り得ない。

　真打劒冑は仕手に装甲されておらずとも、離れ離れ
になっていても、傷の回復を早める程度の真似はする。
　しかしそれは仕手と<ruby>奇<rt>く</rt></ruby>しき<ruby>縁<rt>えにし</rt></ruby>で結ばれていればこそ
の事だ。

　<ruby>帯刀の儀<rt>タテワキ</rt></ruby>と呼ばれる武家古伝の儀礼がある。
　これは武人と劒冑とが対面して互いの資質を問い、
使い手として武器として双方が承認し合う――という
ものである。

en.html:
Only after this rite do warrior and sword-armor become one and are reborn as a warrior with unnatural power. The souls so bound are inseparable; not even ten thousand miles can divide them.

Hikaru could not have done that rite. Not possible.
A person whose mind had shattered, how would any sword-armor accept her as master?

And indeed, Hikaru was still lying in bed.
Body recovered, but no sign of getting up.

en.html:
The sword-armor was the same. Afterwards everyone was confused, but all the same we carried the ceremony through to its end, and sealed it again behind the sacred doors without any incident. All that time, it did not move even a hair.

That Hikaru and that silver sword-armor had formed a bond, I could not believe.

And still, Hikaru's super-recovery could be put down to nothing but a sword-armor's power.

Such a story is in no warrior tradition, east or west, old or new. At least, I had never heard one.

It was beyond understanding.
Maybe that is why I could not feel like leaping with joy, though by rights I should have.

My foster mother seemed to be the same.
The senior house and the other eminent persons had gone home yesterday with anxious faces: they could not say what, but perhaps something ill had happened.

...Truly.
What was that?

en.html:
As if to brush off something clinging to me, I gave one last cut and put the wooden sword away.
Hikaru's body had recovered. That is good. It is a good thing.

But the one involved was a sword-armor. And not any sword-armor: the 'wicked thing' that the Minato house is ordered to keep sealed through past, present and future.

This was what stuck in my mind.
For no reason impatience rose in me, and my heart began to beat too fast.

Good omen? Or bad?
I could not tell yet. It was like staring at the cup that hides the dice in a gambling den.

With gambling, at least, the cup is lifted in the end. The dice decide win or loss.
If this too is gambling... then what number will finally show—

　光の身体が回復した――それは良い。良い事なのだ。

　だが、それに関与したのは劒冑。
　しかも、皆斗家が過去現在未来に渡って封ずるべし
と定められた〝邪しきもの〟だ。

　そこが心に引っ掛かってならない。

　これは吉事か。

　未だ、判然としない。

心地だ。

　賭博であれば、結果は必ず示される。
　出目が勝ち負けを決める。

　これが賭博であるなら……
　果たして、どんな出目が――

Hikaru was there.

In the soft afternoon sunlight, my younger sister stood.

A figure I knew well until a year ago,◆
that became distant in this one year,◆
and that I had longed to see again, even while it blurred bit by bit in my memory.

Hikaru was smiling.

—Hikaru was there.

My sister let me do as I wished.
As though asking a price in return, her fingers touched my hair.

By now nothing else mattered.
So long as this feeling was certain, everything else could go where it liked.

What had brought this, I did not care.
Sword-armor or taboo, either one.

I only gave thanks for this miracle.
Whatever it was, I gave thanks!
en.text:
My sister let me do as I wished.
As though asking a price in return, her fingers touched my hair.

By now nothing else mattered.
So long as this feeling was certain, everything else could go where it liked.

What had brought this, I did not care.
Sword-armor or taboo, either one.

I only gave thanks for this miracle.
Whatever it was, I gave thanks!

I forced my body away from Hikaru and stepped back.

Her eyes were already wet.

en.html:
It was not that rising emotion had struck her in the chest.
When I saw my foster mother's face, I was astonished.

She was bewildered.
This was different from doubting her own eyes before an impossible miracle.

She had accepted her daughter's revival as fact.
And on top of that, something was blocking her plain joy.

What?

...My foster mother was looking at Hikaru.
At Hikaru's face.

Hikaru too was turned toward her mother.
She was letting that expression be seen.

en.html:
Impossible.
Yet however many times I looked again, the shape did not change.

Hikaru smiled her malice.
My foster mother received it without a word.

Never before had such a thing happened.

Before her illness, perhaps because of her age, Hikaru had sometimes been rebellious toward her mother. But not once had she given her this kind of look.

...Perhaps, having just awakened, she was confused somehow.
Unless I thought like that, there was no way to accept it.
